name: Abū al-ʿAbbās Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd ibn Wallād al-Tamīmī
summary: Egyptian grammarian, a student of al-Zajjāj, who answered al-Mubarrad's critique of Sībawayh in al-Intiṣār.
bio: Ibn Wallād came of a family of Egyptian grammarians: their forebear Wallād is the first Egyptian in al-Zubaydī's list, and Abū al-ʿAbbās stands in its third generation with Abū al-Qāsim ibn Wallād of the same family and Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās. He studied in Baghdad with al-Zajjāj and brought his teaching back to Egypt.

His al-Intiṣār li-Sībawayh ʿalā al-Mubarrad takes up the points al-Mubarrad had raised against al-Kitāb and defends Sībawayh one by one; his book on the nouns ending in short and long alif (al-Maqṣūr wa-l-mamdūd) also survives. The sources tell of his rivalry with al-Naḥḥās. He died in 332/944.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 159 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
